code: a <- interval(10, 30) b <- interval(20, 40) intv_union(a, b) #> <interval[1]> #> [1] 10–40 intv_intersection(a, b) #> <interval[1]> #> [1] 20–30

title: Temporal intervals and relations
text: temporal relation mathematical object describing relationship two temporal intervals, defined formal function intervals’ four endpoints (start end ). avoid ambiguities natural language descriptions — example, statements whether two phases “contemporary” can read several different ways, whereas formal relation single, precise meaning. chronological modelling serve exact vocabulary, enabling computational analysis consistent comparison chronological claims across studies. remainder section introduces typology relations implemented tempo Levy et al. (2021); Levy (2025). relation functions share signature fn(x, y, strict = FALSE) accept interval objects, two-element numeric vectors, lists two-element numeric vectors. default, comparisons inclusive (using >= <=). Setting strict = TRUE uses strict comparisons (using > <), affects relations involve equality endpoints. example, two intervals sharing endpoint contemporary_with() default, strict comparison: package provides 24 functions testing temporal relations, listed table order Levy’s typology. Adapted (2025, Table 5). definitions inclusive variants; set strict = TRUE exclusive variants.
code: intv1 <- interval(1500, 1900) intv2 <- interval(1800, 1950) intv3 <- interval(1900, 1950)  contemporary_with(intv1, intv2) #> [1] TRUE  # Inclusive (default): intervals sharing an endpoint are contemporary contemporary_with(intv1, intv3) #> [1] TRUE  # Strict: intervals must overlap in their interiors contemporary_with(intv1, intv3, strict = TRUE) #> [1] FALSE
